page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor with 4 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 15.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA Turing T4 GPU with 16 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear division between CPU-bound tasks and GPU-accelerated workloads. Standard CPU and memory operations, including stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests, consistently score in the lower tiers, often falling into the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth and decompression speeds are similarly limited. Conversely, the integrated NVIDIA T4 GPU delivers strong performance for machine learning tasks. LLM inference benchmarks for small (135M) and medium (7B) models place the instance in the top 10% for prompt processing and the top 25% for text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.gn6i-c4g1.xlarge serves as an entry-level GPU instance. It trades off high-performance general-purpose compute and local storage for cost-effective access to hardware acceleration. This resource profile makes it highly suitable for lightweight deep learning inference, small to medium LLM deployment, and GPU-accelerated graphics rendering, while it is less optimal for CPU-heavy compilation, high-throughput database operations, or memory-intensive caching.
